title: Bethel Defends Democracy: Food Insecurity
description:
Please join us for our 13th consecutive rally to Defend Democracy in beautiful downtown Bethel. While our overall theme is Defending Democracy, each week we pick a specific focus. On Saturday May 31st, 11am -12:30pm, our focus will be on Food Insecurity.

Food insecurity is when people don't have enough to eat and don't know where their next meal will come from. It's a big problem in the United States, where about 47 million people, including about 14 million children, experience food insecurity annually. 

You can be food insecure if you worry about running out of food, are not able to afford balanced meals, or you eat less or skip meals.

People disproportionately impacted by food insecurity include children, many communities of color, households with low incomes, immigrant communities, LGBTQ+ individuals, people with disabilities, people in certain geographies (e.g., rural areas, cities, the South), people who are formerly incarcerated, and single-parent households and many elderly.

Food insecurity exists in every county and congressional district in the U.S.

 Key strategies to address food insecurity include strengthening Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), making free school meals available to all children, expanding access to affordable housing and healthcare, and reducing food waste.   

This is the exact OPPOSITE of what the current administration is doing!!!

Our guest speaker will be Linda Hutchings, the Food Sourcing Manager for Community Food Rescue, a nonprofit organization in Danbury, CT, that works to eliminate hunger in the Greater Danbury area. She is also a key figure in the Community Action Agency of Western Connecticut's efforts to combat food insecurity. Hutchings plays a crucial role in connecting food pantries with food sources, managing food drives, and developing new food banks. She has been instrumental in rescuing food from local stores and partnering with local companies to provide food to those in need. 

Live music will be performed by Erik Rabaska.
Erik Rabasca is a musician, producer, singer/songwriter, founder of the band Light Warriors and the independent label Highest Frequency Records. He plays a fusion of styles as an acoustic soloist ranging from folk, roots and jazz to reggae, indie and even a touch of country. His songwriting has been compared to Bob Dylan and Marley, Paul Simon and more. He has toured the country, performed internationally, opened for Grammy-winners Jon Batiste and Mike Farris, reggae legends Mad Professor, Culture, Sugar Minott, among others, has collaborated with Mad Professor and released over a dozen albums and EPs in various projects (Light Warriors, Lions Gate, Ecstatica, Human Tribes Collective, Other Planes of There, cuebrane) over the last six years alone. He is currently playing in and around the Hudson Valley, NYC and CT. Light Warriors are Ambassadors as part of WhyHunger’s Artists Against Hunger Poverty program.

As part of the Connecticut Hope Collective,  Erik wrote and recorded a song about food insecurity called,  "Just Get To It".  This track was written with the intention of serving some good in the world. 100% of sales will go toward the benefit of the local charity associated through the Pass The Guitar series of concerts. These events bring together 20+ songwriters to raise money for local CT organizations that support hunger and homelessness.

https://theconnecticuthopecollective.bandcamp.com/track/just-get-to-it

The Connecticut Hope Collective is a group of musicians and songwriters who collaborate to create music and events that support local organizations and communities in need. They aim to bring people together and raise awareness for issues like hunger and homelessness while promoting a sense of hope and community. 

The rally is non-partisian. All are welcome.

There will be something for everyone. We'll have speakers, we'll rally with our signs, we'll take a short march and we'll have live music. We also like to end each week with a sing-a-long.

A sign-making table will also be available, complete with all the necessary supplies, for young and old to make signs for the rally.

We also collect a non-perishable food item for our local food pantry each week.  Since our theme this week is food insecurity, please be extra generous if you can and help us fill the bins at our local food pantry.  

Anything you want to contribute is welcome, but 
some special requests from the food pantry include:

-  Spices, Coffee and Baking supplies are always needed.

-   Individually packaged items. so if you bought a variety pack of something like granola bars or instant oatmeal and discovered there's a flavor you won't eat, please give us the individual packs out of box.

-  Empty egg cartons- Any style, so long as they're clean.

-  SMALL empty detergent bottles

Note: Rally is rain or shine.

There are 2 small benches at the square and we will have a limited number of camping chairs. Please bring your own lawn or camping chair if you'd like.

Approximate Rally Schedule:

- 11:00 - 11:15  Assemble and rally at curb (You are welcome to arrive prior to 11:00 for extra curb time)

- 11:15 - 11:45  Speaker(s)

- 11:45 - Noon  Rally at curb with chant leader

- Noon - 12:20  March with chant leader

- 12:20.              Closing Song

- 12:30.              Disperse

We ask that attendees refrain from sign holding or chanting at the curb during our speaking portion of the rally.  We have had issues with speakers being heard because of the increased honking.  It also is a courtesy to the speakers who are often discussing serious and sensitive topics. We are sharing a small square so we need your help to make the rallies comfortable for everyone.

We have tried to arrange the rallies so there is a little something for everyone: chanting,  marching, themes with speakers,  live music,  fun trinkets, sign making.  We appreciate every one of you that attends and we are working hard to bring all of us together to voice our frustrations, build community and also hopefully learn a little something from experts or your fellow neighbors experiences.

We appreciate your understanding and cooperation. ❤️ 

We also ask that you park at one of the four public parking lots. The lot that is very close to the rally location, PT Barnum Square, is behind the municipal center (number 1 on the map you will receive after registration). PT Barnum Square is the triangle shaped area to the far right on the map and in the center of the map.

title: National Update: 2024 Campaign Results & Upcoming Actions
description:
Join Vote Forward Executive Director Yasmin Radjy and Senior Director of Data & Research Emily Wasserman as we announce the results of our 2024 letter writing campaigns and what comes next.

Since the 2024 election, Vote Forward has engaged in rigorous analysis and deep reflection to inform our response to this challenging moment. We’re now ready to debut the results transparently and introduce our next steps. 

Every cycle, Vote Forward runs numerous RCT (randomized controlled trials) to test the effectiveness of our voter turnout programs. Then, in our continued pursuit of innovation and commitment to transparency, we share our learnings with our volunteers and supporters, peer organizations, and the public. 

We know there’s too much at stake to keep doing the same old thing—and figuring out what works in our new political, media, and cultural landscape requires intense evidence-driven experimentation and testing. This is the time for creativity, innovation, and big bets to win the elections that will matter most to the future of democracy.

By embracing what the Vote Forward community does best—developing and testing smart voter contact strategies powered by volunteers and sharing our learnings—we can be part of the solution. RSVP for the call Monday, June 9th at 8pm ET/ 5pm PT.

description:
Dear friends and fellow Democrats,

We’re excited to invite you to come join Multnomah County Democrats in solidarity with Portland Pride as we celebrate over 40 years of LGBTQ+ Pride right here in Portland, Oregon. The event runs from Saturday, July 19th until July 20th, and will be marked by a parade on Sunday that we would love you to come be a part of and march to show your solidarity with your neighbors and friends! 

We need volunteers to staff our booth on the waterfront who will register voters, connect with festival goers, and help spread the word about what we're doing to secure our rights and fight against the constant pressure to rollback progress. We also need folks to march in the parade with out MultDems contingent, celebrating our Pride!

This is a powerful opportunity for us to see each other in person, engage with our community, show off our Democratic pride, and show support for LBGTQ+ people right here in the Pacific Northwest!

# Portland Pride Waterfront Festival

**Saturday, July 19, 2025**  

12:00 PM - 8:00 PM

**Sunday, July 20, 2025** 

11:30 AM - 6:00 PM

[Portland Pride Website](https://portlandpride.org/)

# Portland Pride Parade

**Sunday, July 20, 2025**

Parade begins at **11AM** from the North Park Blocks and ends on Naito Parkway at the Festival

[Parade route information](https://portlandpride.org/parade-contingent-updates)

Let’s make this the biggest MultDems showing yet! We’ll be marching through the heart of Downtown Portland and stationed in the beautiful Tom McCall Waterfront Park to show off our community values and meet and greet members of our vibrant community.

# Booth Location

Booth 217, located nearest Pine Street Gate Entrance

**Note: The Festival doesn't have an entrance fee, but does have a suggested donation of $10** 

Bring your own signs to express yourself, and don’t forget to wear your MultDems gear and Pride flair if you have it! After the parade, stick around for the full Pride Festival, and all the wonderful community members and attractions it has to offer! It’s a great way to meet and get to know other progressive members of our fair city, and to add your voice to the chorus of folks who stand up for the rights of every member of our community!

We look forward to seeing you there as we come together to represent our Democratic values, connect with our community, and express our Pride!

In solidarity,

Multnomah County Democrats

title: Prayer Action: Defend the Constitution
description:
On July 20th at 5 p.m., People of Faith and Union Members across Indiana will gather to demand our elected representatives speak out against the Trump Administration's refusal to honor Court rulings, including the brazen violation of the Supreme Court's 9-0 ruling to facilitate the return of wrongly-detained Union brother, Kilmar Abrego Garcia.

The Trump administration’s disappearance of Kilmar Abrego Garcia to El Salvador is not just a cruel and unlawful attack on our union brother and his family. It’s a violation of Kilmar's constitutional right to due process — threatening the rights of every American and undermining one of the pillars of our democracy.

Unions know that an injury to one is an injury to all, and an attack on the rights of Kilmar and others will lead to everyone’s rights being stripped next. If due process can be taken from one person, it can be taken from all of us.

The rise of authoritarianism is real, and we are fighting back --- as People of Faith, as Hooisers, and as Union Members --- United as Americans!

title: DGI Pride Month June Club Meeting
description:

title: TTL Book Talk:  Arthur Brooks, Love Your Enemies

location.venue: St. Louis County Library - Clark Family Branch

description:
Wonder how we got to such a dysfunctional political climate? Arthur Brooks explains it in this timely book, Love Your Enemies: How Decent People Can Save America From the Culture of Contempt. Though his book was published in 2019, his concerns are accelerating and at a tipping point! Find answers to how we got here and how we can heal the political divide. Join us for an overview and discussion of Arthur Brooks’ informative and essential book!

Protests, strikes, boycotts are all useful tools in our effort to halt efforts to destroy democracy. But, something as powerful, is the simple art of conversation in civil discourse. Like a pebble in the pond, talk can emanate outward, bringing people into action, who might not have a bigger picture. Talk, stories, and recognizing common ground in one another, can get us there.

Overview of the book (Just in case you didn’t get the whole thing read!)

Breakout discussions on chapters that spoke to us most

Practice conversations of how to engage someone of a different political perspective

How to handle a counter protestor - bridging the divide and deescalation

How to talk to others in your own life. - (We all have at least, that one person.)

Next steps . . . A plan to implement what we have learned from Brooks in our own lives
